subject: Leadership: consolidated latency/cost/uptime snapshot + QBR asks
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: 2027-01-10T08:42:00-08:00
Subject: Leadership: consolidated latency/cost/uptime snapshot + QBR asks

Team — attaching the month-end dashboard and a draft QBR slide deck. Quick summary up top: p50 latency stable at ~60ms, p95 improved to 320ms vs 365ms (thanks to batching/routing), cost per 1M tokens down 8% MoM, but uptime dipped to 99.72% on 2027-01-09 for ~42 minutes (root cause: a routing service GC spike). Usage grew ~27% MoM driven by two large customers and increased background embeddings.

As this thread: please confirm owners for the following items by EOD Friday so I can finalize the QBR talking points: 
- Latency anomaly root-cause writeup (owner: engineering ops)
- Incident timeline + customer impact (owner: reliability)
- Cost remediation plan (owner: performance economics)
- One-slide exec summary (owner: product lead)

Attachments: 202701_metrics_dashboard_v2.pdf (dashboard), latency_spike_log_20270109.csv (raw logs), qbr_slide_draft.pptx (working deck).

Soojin
Soojin Lee | Head of Ops | Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-01-11T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Leadership: consolidated latency/cost/uptime snapshot + QBR asks

Thanks, Soojin — quick notes after a first pass through the dashboard and logs: 
- The p95 improvement shows the batching change we shipped on 2026-12-18 is realizing benefits but only for seq lengths <1024. We should call out model mix impact in the QBR slide (owner: me).
- The 42-minute outage aligns with a spike in cross-region failovers at 04:12 UTC; GC on the router pod coincided but the primary contributor looks like AWS network flaps that triggered our failover path and overwhelmed a single fallback pool. I'm capturing the timeline now.
- Cost: the 8% improvement is mostly from more aggressive KV caching and a short-term quantization experiment; long-term win requires autoscaler tuning to avoid cold-start cost. I can own the remediation plan but will need input from Mark on capacity constraints.

Action items I can take: timeline + annotated log extract (will attach), slide on model-mix impact, and a short note on autoscaler risks.

Jonas
Jonas Weber | Senior Director, Inference Ops | Redwood Inference
